# Cadence UI — full context

# Cadence UI

> Animation-first React components for shadcn. Base UI + Tailwind CSS v4 + Motion.
> Install with `npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/<id>`. Every component ships its motion contract and a reduced-motion branch.

## Install

```json
{ "registries": { "@cadence": "https://cadence.dev/r/{name}.json" } }
```

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/fade-in
```

## Rules for agents

- Prefer an existing Cadence component over writing new animation code.
- Read the item's `docs` and `meta.motion` before changing motion.
- Keep the reduced-motion branch; never remove `data-motion`.
- Use presets from `components/cadence/lib/motion.ts`; do not invent durations.

## Components

- [Fade in](/r/fade-in.md): Reveal content on scroll with a short rise and a reduced-motion fallback. (text, motion)
- [Text reveal](/r/text-reveal.md): Reveal a heading or paragraph word by word, with a single accessible sentence. (text, motion)
- [Number flow](/r/number-flow.md): A number that rolls from its previous value to the next, with a static accessible value. (feedback, motion)
- [Morph button](/r/morph-button.md): A button whose label and width morph between idle, loading, success, and error. (feedback, motion)
- [Animated tabs](/r/animated-tabs.md): Tabs with a shared-element indicator and an animated panel swap. (navigation, motion)
- [Motion accordion](/r/motion-accordion.md): An accordion whose panels spring open and closed, with a rotating chevron. (navigation, motion)
- [Scroll progress](/r/scroll-progress.md): A reading-progress bar that follows the page scroll on a spring. (scroll, motion)
- [Motion dialog](/r/motion-dialog.md): A Base UI dialog whose panel rises and settles on a spring, interruptible mid-exit. (overlay, motion)

## Docs

- [/r/registry.json](/r/registry.json): install index
- [/r/catalog.json](/r/catalog.json): machine-readable catalog
- [/llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt): every component doc inline


---

# Fade in

Reveal content on scroll with a short rise and a reduced-motion fallback.

## When to use

- Section intros, cards, and empty states that should arrive when they enter the viewport.
- Anywhere you want one consistent entrance instead of hand-writing `whileInView` per element.
- Marketing pages where a short rise adds reading rhythm without delaying content.

## When not to use

- Content that is already visible on first paint and must not move (use no animation).
- Long lists where every row would animate at once; use a stagger container instead.
- Replacing layout or routing transitions; this only animates its own children.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/fade-in
```

This pulls in `cadence-motion`, `cadence-utils`, and `cadence-provider` automatically.

## Usage

```tsx
import { FadeIn } from "@/components/cadence/fade-in/fade-in";

export function Feature() {
  return (
    <FadeIn distance={16} delay={0.05}>
      <h2>Everything you need to ship</h2>
    </FadeIn>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Stagger a row of cards

```tsx
<div className="grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-3">
  {features.map((feature, index) => (
    <FadeIn key={feature.title} delay={index * 0.06}>
      <Card {...feature} />
    </FadeIn>
  ))}
</div>
```

### Replay on every entry

```tsx
<FadeIn once={false} distance={24}>
  <Quote />
</FadeIn>
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Stagger offset in seconds. Ignored when motion is reduced. |
| `distance` | `number` | `12` | Pixels travelled while fading in. |
| `once` | `boolean` | `true` | Reveal once, or replay on every viewport entry. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged with the wrapper classes. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | – | Content to reveal. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | `opacity 0 → 1`, `translateY distance → 0` | `reveal` (0.22s, ease-out) | n/a (one-shot) |
| reduced | `opacity` only, 0.16s | `reveal` short | n/a |
| none | end state immediately | – | n/a |

## Keyboard interactions

No keyboard behaviour of its own. Focus order and semantics are unchanged.

## Accessibility

- Never hides content permanently: opacity reaches `1` and the element stays in the DOM.
- The wrapper is a `div`; pass `as`-style semantics by nesting the correct element, or use your own wrapper.
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`; with reduce enabled only opacity animates.

## Responsive behavior

Distance is in pixels, not viewport units, so the motion stays subtle on mobile. Use a larger
`distance` only for full-width hero blocks.

## Performance

- Animates `opacity` and `transform` only, on the compositor.
- One `IntersectionObserver` per instance, no scroll listeners.
- Prefer `once` for long pages so observers disconnect after the first reveal.

## Notes for AI

- Default entrance for a single block. For lists, keep the stagger on the parent and use small values (≤ 0.06s per item).
- Do not wrap above-the-fold hero text that must be readable before hydration.
- If the design already animates the parent, nest `FadeIn` only for the child that needs its own timing.

# Text reveal

Reveal a heading or paragraph word by word, with a single accessible sentence.

## When to use

- Page titles and section headings that deserve a moment of arrival.
- Short paragraphs (under ~40 words) where per-word rhythm reads as intentional.
- Landing pages where the copy is the main visual.

## When not to use

- Body copy people scan or re-read; per-word motion slows reading.
- Text that changes often (live data, counters); use a number component instead.
- Content with inline links, emphasis, or icons: this component takes a plain string only.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/text-reveal
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { TextReveal } from "@/components/cadence/text-reveal/text-reveal";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <TextReveal as="h1" stagger={0.04}>
      Motion that explains what just happened
    </TextReveal>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Slower, heavier entrance

```tsx
<TextReveal as="h2" stagger={0.08} delay={0.1}>
  Built for products, not demos
</TextReveal>
```

### Reduce to a single fade

Set `data-motion="reduced"` on an ancestor (or enable the OS setting) and the whole string
fades once instead of word by word.

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `string` | – | Plain text. Inline markup is not supported. |
| `as` | `"h1" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "p" \| "span"` | `"p"` | Semantic element. |
| `stagger` | `number` | `0.035` | Seconds between words. |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Seconds before the first word. |
| `once` | `boolean` | `true` | Reveal once or replay on entry. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged onto the semantic element. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | per word `opacity 0 → 1`, `translateY 0.35em → 0` | `text.reveal` (0.32s, stagger 0.035s) | n/a |
| reduced | whole string fades once | `reveal` | n/a |
| none | end state immediately | – | n/a |

## Keyboard interactions

None. Text is not interactive and does not enter the tab order.

## Accessibility

- The visible words are `aria-hidden`; the element itself carries `aria-label` with the full string,
  so screen readers announce the sentence once.
- The rendered element keeps its heading/paragraph role, so document structure is preserved.
- Reduced motion swaps the stagger for one fade; no content is delayed or hidden.

## Responsive behavior

Works at any width. Very narrow columns can produce many short lines; lower `stagger` to keep the
total under ~0.4s.

## Performance

- One span per word. Keep strings short; a 200-word paragraph creates 200 elements.
- Animates opacity and transform only.
- Splitting happens during render, so the DOM is stable after hydration.

## Notes for AI

- Only pass plain strings. If the copy needs a link or `<strong>`, split the sentence and wrap parts
  in separate `TextReveal` instances instead of injecting markup.
- Keep total stagger (`stagger × words`) under 0.4s.
- Do not use for navigation labels or buttons.

# Number flow

A number that rolls from its previous value to the next, with a static accessible value.

## When to use

- Metrics, KPIs, and totals that update while the user watches.
- Prices and counters where a jump would hide the direction of the change.
- Dashboard cards that refresh on an interval or a filter change.

## When not to use

- Currency inputs the user types into; use a controlled input.
- Values that change several times per second (streams, live tickers); the spring never settles.
- Numbers that must be copyable as text; the rendered frames are not stable text.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/number-flow
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { NumberFlow } from "@/components/cadence/number-flow/number-flow";

export function Revenue({ value }: { value: number }) {
  return <NumberFlow value={value} prefix="$" precision={0} announce />;
}
```

## Examples

### Percentage with one decimal

```tsx
<NumberFlow value={0.873} precision={1} suffix="%" />
```

### Localized grouping

```tsx
<NumberFlow value={1234567} locale="de-DE" />
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | – | The value to display. Changes animate. |
| `precision` | `number` | `0` | Fraction digits. |
| `locale` | `string` | runtime | Locale passed to `Intl.NumberFormat`. |
| `prefix` / `suffix` | `string` | – | Rendered beside the number, outside the animated value. |
| `announce` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds `aria-live="polite"` for result-style values. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged onto the wrapper. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | spring from old to new value, formatted per frame | `number.roll` (0.26s spring) | yes |
| reduced | new value shown directly | – | – |
| none | new value shown directly | – | – |

## Keyboard interactions

None. Not focusable.

## Accessibility

- The element exposes the final formatted value through `aria-label`; intermediate frames stay out of
  the accessibility tree.
- `announce` adds a polite live region for results such as a checkout total. Leave it off for counters
  that change often, or screen readers will chatter.
- Tabular numbers keep the width stable as digits change.

## Responsive behavior

Uses `tabular-nums` and inline flow, so it inherits font size from the container. For very large
numbers, reduce `precision` rather than shrinking the font.

## Performance

- One spring per instance; updates are cheap and do not re-render React.
- Avoid dozens of these on one screen; each runs a frame loop while settling.

## Notes for AI

- Use for numbers that change in place. For editable numbers use an input, for static values use text.
- Keep `announce` off unless the number is a result the user is waiting for.
- Never format inside the parent and pass a string; pass the raw number so the spring can interpolate.

# Morph button

A button whose label and width morph between idle, loading, success, and error.

## When to use

- Forms where a submit button changes to loading, then success, then back.
- Toolbars where the label changes in place ("Save" → "Saved") and the button should keep its width.
- Any action where the button itself can carry the result without a toast.

## When not to use

- Navigation links; use a link component.
- Destructive actions that need a confirmation step; use a dialog or a hold-to-confirm pattern.
- Buttons whose label does not change; a plain button is lighter.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/morph-button
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { MorphButton } from "@/components/cadence/morph-button/morph-button";

export function SaveBar({ save }: { save: () => Promise<void> }) {
  const [state, setState] = React.useState<"idle" | "loading" | "success">("idle");
  return (
    <MorphButton
      state={state}
      labels={{ idle: "Save changes", loading: "Saving", success: "Saved" }}
      onClick={async () => {
        setState("loading");
        await save();
        setState("success");
      }}
    >
      Save changes
    </MorphButton>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Error recovery

```tsx
<MorphButton
  state={status}
  labels={{ loading: "Sending", error: "Try again", success: "Sent" }}
  variant={status === "error" ? "danger" : "primary"}
>
  Send invite
</MorphButton>
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `"idle" \| "loading" \| "success" \| "error"` | `"idle"` | Visible state; drives icon and label. |
| `labels` | `Partial<Record<State, ReactNode>>` | – | Label per state. Falls back to `children`. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "danger"` | `"primary"` | Visual weight. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Height and padding. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged onto the button. |
| `...props` | `ButtonHTMLAttributes` | – | Forwarded to the underlying button. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| state change | label `opacity`/`translateY 4px`, slot `width → auto` | `state.morph` (0.42s spring, no overshoot) | yes |
| press | `scale 0.97` (icon sizes slightly less) | `feedback.press` (0.24s spring) | yes |
| reduced | label crossfade only; width jumps; no press scale | `state.morph` short | yes |
| none | instant label swap | – | – |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Activates the button. |
| Tab | Focuses the button; loading keeps it focusable. |

## Accessibility

- Loading uses `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled`, so keyboard focus is not lost mid-action.
- Clicks are swallowed while loading, but the button stays focusable.
- Success and error are announced through a visually hidden `role="status"` live region.
- Icon-only usage needs an `aria-label`; the icon is `aria-hidden`.

## Responsive behavior

Width springs to the measured label width, so the button never clips on narrow screens. If the label
wraps, the measurement follows the new height without animating it.

## Performance

- One `ResizeObserver` per button, disconnected on unmount.
- Animates opacity, transform, and the slot width (layout) only on state changes, not continuously.
- The spinner is a CSS rotation; reduced motion renders it static.

## Notes for AI

- Drive `state` from your request state; do not fake success before the promise resolves.
- Keep labels short; the width animation is meant for a few words, not a sentence.
- Use `variant="danger"` for error only if the action itself is destructive; otherwise keep the variant stable.

# Animated tabs

Tabs with a shared-element indicator and an animated panel swap.

## When to use

- Two to six peer views in the same context (overview, activity, settings).
- Panels whose content is lightweight enough to mount on selection.
- Anywhere the active indicator is part of the design language.

## When not to use

- More than ~7 sections; use a sidebar or select.
- Content that must keep its state while hidden (a form being edited in another tab); keep the
  panels mounted yourself or use a router.
- Navigation between routes; use links with `aria-current`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/animated-tabs
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { AnimatedTabs } from "@/components/cadence/animated-tabs/animated-tabs";

export function Settings() {
  return (
    <AnimatedTabs
      defaultValue="profile"
      items={[
        { value: "profile", label: "Profile", content: <ProfileForm /> },
        { value: "billing", label: "Billing", content: <Billing /> },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `AnimatedTabItem[]` | – | `value`, `label`, `content`, optional `disabled`. |
| `value` | `string` | – | Controlled active value. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | first enabled | Initial value when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | – | Called on click and keyboard selection. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged onto the root. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| indicator | shared-element FLIP between tabs | `layout.shared` (0.42s spring) | yes |
| panel in | `opacity`, `translateY 8px to 0` | `reveal` | n/a (mount only) |
| reduced | indicator jumps, panel fades only | `reveal` short | yes |
| none | instant swap | – | – |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus into the tab list (roving tabindex). |
| Arrow Right / Left | Moves to the next/previous enabled tab and activates it. |
| Home / End | First/last enabled tab. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused tab (already activated on focus). |

## Accessibility

- Implements the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, `role="tabpanel"`,
  `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`, roving `tabIndex`.
- The panel is focusable (`tabIndex={0}`) so keyboard users can scroll long content.
- Disabled tabs are skipped by arrow navigation.

## Responsive behavior

The list scrolls horizontally only if you add `overflow-x-auto`; by default it wraps. For narrow
screens keep labels short or switch to a select.

## Performance

- Only the active panel is mounted; switching unmounts the previous one (state resets).
- The indicator uses Motion's layout projection, which measures once per switch.

## Notes for AI

- Keep panel content cheap; it mounts on every switch.
- If a panel holds form state, lift it up or use a router instead of tabs.
- Do not add `layout` animations inside the panel; they will fight the shared indicator.

# Motion accordion

An accordion whose panels spring open and closed, with a rotating chevron.

## When to use

- FAQ sections and settings groups where one answer is open at a time.
- Long forms split into optional sections.
- Any disclosure where the height change should feel physical rather than instant.

## When not to use

- Primary navigation (use a menu).
- Content that must always be visible for SEO-critical copy; render it open by default.
- Nested accordions more than two levels deep; the height animation compounds.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/motion-accordion
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { MotionAccordion } from "@/components/cadence/motion-accordion/motion-accordion";

export function Faq() {
  return (
    <MotionAccordion
      defaultValue="billing"
      items={[
        { value: "billing", trigger: "How does billing work?", content: "We bill monthly." },
        { value: "cancel", trigger: "Can I cancel?", content: "Any time, from settings." },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `AccordionItem[]` | – | `value`, `trigger`, `content`. |
| `type` | `"single" \| "multiple"` | `"single"` | One open panel, or any number. |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` | – | Controlled / initial open values. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string \| string[]) => void` | – | Called with a string in single mode. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `true` | Allow closing the open panel in single mode. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged onto the root. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | `height 0 → auto`, content `opacity`/`translateY 4px` | `state.morph` (0.42s spring) | yes |
| close | reverse of open | `state.morph` | yes |
| chevron | `rotate 0 → 180°` | `state.morph` on open, `exit.fade` on close | yes |
| reduced | height snaps, content fades | `state.morph` short | yes |
| none | instant | – | – |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Toggles the focused trigger. |
| Tab | Moves through triggers and open panel content. |

## Accessibility

- Triggers are native buttons with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
- Open panels are `role="region"` labelled by their trigger, and are removed from the DOM when closed.
- Chevron is decorative (`aria-hidden`); the expanded state is conveyed by `aria-expanded`.

## Responsive behavior

Height animates to `auto`, so content of any length works. On very long panels the spring can feel
slow; reduce content or switch `type="multiple"` and keep one open.

## Performance

- Animating `height` triggers layout on each frame. Keep panels under ~600px tall.
- Content is mounted only while open, so collapsed sections cost nothing.

## Notes for AI

- Use `type="multiple"` only when sections are independent.
- Do not put another accordion inside a panel unless you disable height animation; nested height
  springs beat against each other.
- Keep trigger labels as plain text; the whole button is the hit target.

# Scroll progress

A reading-progress bar that follows the page scroll on a spring.

## When to use

- Long-form articles, documentation pages, and changelogs.
- Any page where "how much is left" helps orientation.
- As a global indicator mounted once in the root layout.

## When not to use

- Short pages that fit in one viewport; the bar never moves.
- App shells with their own scroll containers (the hook tracks the window by default).
- As a substitute for a table of contents or section navigation.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/scroll-progress
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { ScrollProgress } from "@/components/cadence/scroll-progress/scroll-progress";

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <>
      <ScrollProgress />
      {children}
    </>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Bottom-aligned, thicker bar

```tsx
<ScrollProgress position="bottom" height={3} className="bg-primary" />
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `height` | `number` | `2` | Bar thickness in px. |
| `position` | `"top" \| "bottom"` | `"top"` | Viewport edge to pin to. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged onto the bar; use it to change the color. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| scroll | `scaleX` follows `scrollYProgress` with a spring | `scroll.progress` (0.4s spring) | yes (continuous) |
| reduced | raw progress, no spring | – | – |
| none | raw progress | – | – |

## Keyboard interactions

None. The bar is decorative and not focusable.

## Accessibility

- `aria-hidden="true"`: the progress is visual only and adds no noise for screen readers.
- Hidden in print styles.
- `pointer-events-none`: it never blocks clicks near the viewport edge.

## Responsive behavior

Full viewport width, fixed position. On mobile browsers with a dynamic toolbar the bar stays pinned
because it uses `fixed` rather than absolute positioning.

## Performance

- One `scrollYProgress` listener; the transform is compositor-only.
- The spring adds a frame loop only while scrolling.

## Notes for AI

- Mount once, at the layout level, not per page.
- For a scroll container other than the window, pass a custom `useScroll` target in your own wrapper;
  this component intentionally stays window-scoped and dependency-free.
- Do not use it as a loading indicator.

# Motion dialog

A Base UI dialog whose panel rises and settles on a spring, interruptible mid-exit.

## When to use

- A focused task that must interrupt: confirmations, short forms, destructive actions.
- Content that needs a modal, focus trapping, and a clear escape route.
- Any overlay where closing should feel like the panel "settles back" rather than vanishing.

## When not to use

- Non-blocking hints and menus; use a popover or tooltip.
- Long multi-step flows; use a page or a wizard.
- Mobile sheets with drag gestures; use a drawer component.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/motion-dialog
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { MotionDialog } from "@/components/cadence/motion-dialog/motion-dialog";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <MotionDialog
      trigger="Delete project"
      title="Delete this project?"
      description="This removes every deployment and cannot be undone."
    >
      <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
        <button className="rounded-md border border-border px-3 py-2 text-sm">Cancel</button>
        <button className="rounded-md bg-destructive px-3 py-2 text-sm text-white">Delete</button>
      </div>
    </MotionDialog>
  );
}
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | `ReactNode` | – | Content of the trigger button. |
| `title` | `string` | – | Dialog title; required for accessibility. |
| `description` | `string` | – | Optional supporting text. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | – | Dialog body. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Max width. |
| `open` | `boolean` | – | Controlled open state. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | – | Called on open and close. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged onto the panel. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | backdrop `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity`, `translateY 8px → 0`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `popup.anchored` (0.4s spring) | yes |
| exit | panel `opacity → 0`, `scale → 0.98`, `translateY 4px` | `popup.anchored` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only | `exit.fade` / `popup.anchored` short | yes |
| none | instant | – | – |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. |
| Escape | Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides the modal semantics: `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` /
  `aria-describedby`, focus trap, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling.
- The close button has an explicit `aria-label`.
- The title is required; a dialog without an accessible name is invalid.
- The panel is removed only after its exit animation finishes, so focus is never lost mid-flight.

## Responsive behavior

The viewport centers the panel and scrolls when the content is taller than the screen. `size` caps the
width; on mobile the panel is always full-width minus page padding.

## Performance

- Only one panel tree is mounted while open; content is unmounted on close.
- Animates opacity and transform only; the backdrop uses a subtle blur (2px), which is cheap but can
  be removed on low-end devices.

## Notes for AI

- Always pass a `title`; it is the accessible name.
- For destructive actions, keep the confirm button's label specific ("Delete project", not "OK").
- If you need a non-modal popover, use Base UI Popover instead of this component.
